key_insight: Asymmetric electron–defect scattering can generate a large extrinsic photovoltaic current that peaks at a finite defect fraction.
engineering_relevance: Controlling defect type and concentration could provide a tunable route to stronger photovoltaic responses in monolayer GeS.
method: Apply an ab initio Boltzmann framework to monolayer GeS.
Combine optical excitation with electron–phonon scattering.
Include symmetric and skew electron–defect scattering.
evidence_signal: The scattering-limited calculations predict over six orders of magnitude enhancement upon cooling to 0 K at fixed defect fraction, with extrinsic current exceeding intrinsic shift current by over tenfold at selected low-temperature defect fractions.
watch_item: The largest enhancements are low-temperature model predictions; practical gains require experimental validation and controlled defect populations.
paper_title: Extrinsic Bulk Photovoltaic Effect from Asymmetric Defect Scattering
